Twelve comments

Contentment Is Wealth (jig)

There are 2 distinct (or distantly related?) tunes known by this name, but I believe this is the more common one. I picked it up from the playing of Leeds Ceili Band recorded more than 10 years ago. Brian Rooney recorded a very similar version on the box, citing Paddy Killoran as the source.

↳ Posted by slainte on February 20th, 2007.

I’ve just found Paddy O’Brien’s setting of this tune here: https://thesession.org/tunes/1662#comment29254 It deserves a separate post!

↳ Posted by slainte on February 20th, 2007.

The other one’s more common in sessions I go to.

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on February 21st, 2007.

The other “Contentment is Wealth” Jig at
https://thesession.org/tunes/1662

is IMHO very similar - maybe a nice setting to play these two as a four part jig?

↳ Posted by swisspiper on February 21st, 2007.

Keyboard

If a Cape Bretoner tells you to play the Golden Keyboard, they mean this one.

↳ Posted by DonallDubh on May 24th, 2009.

No. The other “Contentment is Wealth” is the one played as “the Golden Keyboard” in Cape Breton.

↳ Posted by slainte on May 25th, 2009.

Contentment Is Wealth, X:4

Taken from ‘A Fine Selection of Over 200 Irish Traditional Tunes for Sessions’, compiled by David Speers with a Forward by Matt Cranitch. This setting doesn’t have the octave leap in the first bar which, I think, makes those in the third and fourth bars a bit more of a contrast.

↳ Posted by Eubonian on January 4th, 2019.

Re: Contentment Is Wealth

A lovely jig, very closely related to “The Lumps of Pudding” in the English tradition--used by John Gay as the tune to the last song in "The Beggar’s Opera.

↳ Posted by John Mullen on August 19th, 2021.

The first jig I’ve really fallen in love with. Joe McKenna does a really great recording on the album “The Irish Low Whistle,” with some nice ornamentation and interesting inversions.

↳ Posted by algannaio on May 5th, 2022.
